water.name: Land
water.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points (centre + 6) fall on a gmina (GISCO LAU) or a neighbouring country (Natural Earth), unless the centre is sea and the ETOPO 2022 mean is at or below sea level, or at least half its ETOPO samples are.

water.name: Open sea
water.rule: Baltic deeper than 40 m and not next to land.

water.name: Coastal water
water.rule: Sea or lagoon next to a land hex, or shallower than 40 m (ETOPO 2022 mean). The Szczecin, Vistula and Curonian lagoons are coastal water.

water.name: Lake
water.rule: At least half of the hex's land-cover points are permanent water (ESA WorldCover 2021) and the water surface is above sea level (ETOPO 2022). A lake hex next to the sea stays a lake only where Natural Earth has a lake (Łebsko); otherwise it is a lagoon (coastal water).

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 28 m.

relief.name: Hills
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation of 28 m or more (moraine hills, uplands).

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation of 110 m or more, or mean elevation of 750 m or more.

relief.name: Peaks
relief.rule: Mountains whose highest sample reaches 1,450 m, above the tree line (the Tatra, Babia Góra, Pilsko, the Karkonosze with Śnieżka).

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, or no WorldCover land points.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Tree cover (WorldCover 10) is the largest group and broad-leaved forest the largest forest type (Copernicus forest type layer 2019).

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: Tree cover is the largest group and needle-leaved forest (pine, spruce, larch) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Tree cover is the largest group and mixed forest the largest forest type, or the type is unknown.

cover.name: Mountain meadows
cover.rule: Grassland (30) or moss and lichen (100) is the largest group in a hex 900 m or higher: mountain meadows and alpine grass.

cover.name: Meadows and pastures
cover.rule: Grassland (WorldCover 30) is the largest group in a hex under 900 m. In lowland Poland this class is mostly hay meadows and pastures.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: Herbaceous wetland (WorldCover 90: fens, reed beds, river marshes) is the largest group.

cover.name: Built-up
cover.rule: Built-up land (WorldCover 50) is 28% or more of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

cover.name: Bare rock and sand
cover.rule: Bare or sparse vegetation (60: rock, dunes, quarries) is the largest group.

cover.name: Snow and ice
cover.rule: Permanent snow and ice (70) is the largest group.

notes.water: Gmina outlines (GISCO LAU 2024, 1:1 million) and Natural Earth 1:10m country outlines do not meet exactly. A sea hex whose ETOPO 2022 mean is above sea level (and under half of its samples below it) becomes land when at least 4 of its 6 neighbours are land, or when it touches both Polish and foreign land; it takes the neighbours' majority owner. Lakes and the land of spits narrower than a hex (the Hel Peninsula, the Vistula Spit) are drawn as outlines over the hexes (world.json lakes and spits). A sea hex's elevation is the mean of its ETOPO samples below sea level (its water depth).
notes.relief: From ETOPO 2022 samples (15 arc-second, about 460 m by 290 m, roughly 300 per hex) at -30 m or higher, so lagoons and sea floor do not count; all samples are used if none qualify. Water hexes are always flat. A hex whose lower 60% of samples is flat lowland (spread under 15 m, under 300 m) is eased one class.
notes.cover: From ESA WorldCover 2021 (read at 1/375 degree, about 300 m by 180 m), sampled on a 450 m lattice inside each hex (about 320 points). Water and no-data points are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points, rounded to whole percent, and the built-up threshold is applied to the rounded share. The forest type (conifer, deciduous, mixed) is the most common type of the Copernicus Global Land Cover 2019 forest layer at the hex's tree points. Neighbouring countries get a cover class for the map art; their shares (pct) stay 0.
